{"name": "Jupiter Cloud Layer", "subtitle": "", "body": "(Note: toggle off the cloud layer in the legend to better see the interior structure.)

Jupiter's visible cloud layer consists of bands of different colors, caused by
variations in chemical composition and atmospheric dynamics. The clouds are primarily
composed of ammonia, ammonium hydrosulfide, and water. The famous Great Red Spot
is a massive storm system located in this layer. Temperature ranges from 120 K in
the highest ammonia ice clouds to about 200 K in the lower ammonium hydrosulfide clouds."}

Jupiter Cloud Layer
(Note: toggle off the cloud layer in the legend to better see the interior structure.)

Jupiter's visible cloud layer consists of bands of different colors, caused by
variations in chemical composition and atmospheric dynamics. The clouds are primarily
composed of ammonia, ammonium hydrosulfide, and water. The famous Great Red Spot
is a massive storm system located in this layer. Temperature ranges from 120 K in
the highest ammonia ice clouds to about 200 K in the lower ammonium hydrosulfide clouds.

the highest ammonia ice clouds to about 200 K in the lower ammonium hydrosulfide clouds.

text:
Jupiter's upper atmosphere includes the stratosphere and thermosphere.
It's less dense than the cloud layer below and contains hydrocarbon haze
produced by solar ultraviolet radiation. Aurora activity can be observed
at Jupiter's poles, caused by interactions with its magnetic field. Temperature
ranges from 200K in the stratosphere to 1000K in the thermosphere and exosphere.

{"name": "New Horizons Jupiter Gravity Assist", "subtitle": "", "body": "Date: 2007-02-28 05:43:40 UTC
Distance: 0.01541 AU (2.31 million km)
Velocity relative to Jupiter: 21.22 km/s
Velocity relative to Sun: 23.00 km/s
Type: Gravity Assist

Fastest launch ever: 16.26 km/s Earth-relative,
combining with Earth's orbital velocity to ~43
km/s heliocentric (velocities add as vectors, not
scalars). The Sun's gravity steadily slowed it to
~19 km/s by Jupiter. The gravity assist added ~4
km/s, boosting speed to ~23 km/s -- partially
recovering what the Sun took. Without this boost,
Pluto arrival would have been three years later.

Source: NASA/JPL"}
data.name: New Horizons Jupiter Gravity Assist
text:
New Horizons Jupiter Gravity Assist
Date: 2007-02-28 05:43:40 UTC
Distance: 0.01541 AU (2.31 million km)
Velocity relative to Jupiter: 21.22 km/s
Velocity relative to Sun: 23.00 km/s
Type: Gravity Assist

Fastest launch ever: 16.26 km/s Earth-relative,
combining with Earth's orbital velocity to ~43
km/s heliocentric (velocities add as vectors, not
scalars). The Sun's gravity steadily slowed it to
~19 km/s by Jupiter. The gravity assist added ~4
km/s, boosting speed to ~23 km/s -- partially
recovering what the Sun took. Without this boost,
Pluto arrival would have been three years later.

Source: NASA/JPL

_encyclopedia.Callisto: Horizons: 504. Jupiter moon. Heavily cratered and geologically inactive.
_encyclopedia.Europa: Horizons: 502. Jupiter moon. Covered with a smooth ice layer, potential subsurface ocean.
_encyclopedia.New Horizons:
***SET MANUAL SCALE TO 0.0003 AU TO PLOT NEW HORIZONS-ARROKOTH FLYBY ON 2019-1-1.

Horizons: -98. New Horizons flew past Pluto in 2015, now exploring the Kuiper Belt.
* The New Horizons space probe is an interplanetary space probe built by the Applied Physics Laboratory of Johns Hopkins
University for NASA.
* It was launched on January 19, 2006 with the primary mission to conduct a flyby study of Pluto and its moons in the Kuiper Belt. It is the first spacecraft to explore Pluto and the Kuiper Belt up close.
* Approaches 2002 JF56 on June 13, 2006 to within 102,000 km at 10:06 UTC
* Jupiter gravity assist on February 28, 2007, 05:43 UTC, 2.3045(10)^6 km
* Pluto Flyby: On July 14, 2015, Pluto-Charon encounter at 11:49:57 UTC. New Horizons made its historic closest approach to Pluto, capturing stunning images and valuable scientific data about the dwarf planet and its moons.
* Kuiper Belt Exploration: After its Pluto encounter, New Horizons continued its journey into the Kuiper Belt.
* Arrokoth (2014 MU69) flyby on January 1, 2019, at 3537.7 km, at 5:34:31 UTC.
* Scientific Instruments: New Horizons carries a suite of scientific instruments, including cameras, spectrometers, and plasma analyzers, to study the composition, atmosphere, and environment of Pluto and other Kuiper Belt objects.
* Continuing Mission: New Horizons is still traveling through the Kuiper Belt, and NASA may extend its mission to explore other distant objects in the future.
_encyclopedia.Amalthea: Horizons: 505. Jupiter moon. Oddly shaped red moon associated with the Amalthea Gossamer Ring.
_encyclopedia.Metis: Horizons: 516. Jupiter moon. Innermost known moon, orbits within Jupiter's main ring, contributing dust to it.
_encyclopedia.Io: Horizons: 501. Jupiter moon. The most volcanically active body in the Solar System.
_encyclopedia.Adrastea: Horizons: 515. Jupiter moon. Tiny moon orbiting near the outer edge of Jupiter's main ring, source of ring material.
_encyclopedia.Thebe: Horizons: 514. Jupiter moon. Small irregular moon that supplies dust to the outermost Thebe Gossamer Ring.
_encyclopedia.Ganymede: Horizons: 503. Jupiter moon. The largest moon in the Solar System, bigger than Mercury.
